jobs.title: Operations Strategy Consultant - FSP Team (AD Level Role)
jobs.description:
Work Schedule
Standard (Mon-Fri)
Environmental Conditions
Office
Job Description

Position requires global clinical trial project management experience, with ideal candidate having experience with proposals and bid defenses. This is an Associate Director level position seeking a candidate with leadership level strategy execution and critical thinking skills.

Join Us as a Operations Strategy Consultant (Associate Director Level Role) – Make an Impact at the Forefront of Innovation

Contributes to the overall success of the proposal development process from receipt through client decision, in order to increase the RFP hit rate and positively impact business growth; through recommendation and implementation of operational strategy for proposal, bid defense, accountability for all related deliverables and successful management of the process. Leverages all opportunities to achieve targets while enhancing customer relations. Primarily responsible for RFPs and supplemental documents for single or multi service/region clinical development protocols or programs and simple to moderate RFIs.

What You'll Do:
- Identifies and recommends operational proposal strategic plans for assigned area (TA or Segment) that align with commercial win strategy; determines the level of proposal deliverable and key operations messages, and manages the triage process within clinical operations to meet proposal deliverables.

- Ensures budget reflects operational strategy and oversees achievement of profitability targets.

- Partners with Clinical operations, Commercial organization and GPD to enhance proposal efficiency management in order to decrease COS.

- Drives the development of the operations segment of the proposal deliverable within prescribed timelines, disseminates operational strategy to proposal team and develops KPI's, ensuring a successful operations segment of the deliverable.

- Collaborates with the cross functional team in matrix environment to establish an efficient and aligned process within clinical operations.

- Manages operations escalation process and advises commercial strategy team.

- Assesses cross functional satisfaction and recommends future strategy and actions to ensure the overall success of the process and outcomes.

- Recommends and implements revisions for Clinical Operations post-award to successfully execute proposal.

Education and Experience Requirements:
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent and relevant formal academic / vocational qualification

- Previous experience that provides the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the job (comparable to 12+ years’) or equivalent combination of education, training, & experience.

Years of experience refers to typical years of related experience needed to gain the required knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the essential functions of the job. Years of experience are not to be used as the only determining factor in establishing the job class or making employment selection decisions.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities:
- Has ability to persuade, convince and influence/impress others, demonstrating leadership capability

- Working knowledge and understanding of clinical project management, the business organization and functional areas

- Possesses cultural awareness and sensitivity, sound interpersonal skills, is flexible and able to adapt to changing situation, customer relationship management skills. Demonstrates strong commercial awareness

- Organized, proficient at multi tasking, with excellent attention to detail. Ability to work in a high pressure/time sensitive environment, capability to handle multiple issues on multiple projects simultaneously

- Demonstrates solid experience/proficiency in proposal development, demonstrated project management and planning skills

- Experience of leading, liaising and coordinating with cross functional teams. Able to aply range of negotiation skills and techniques to achieve results

- Collaborates and builds peer and effective team relationships, able to motivate, evidene of coaching and mentoring skills

- Demonstrates analytical skills, effective oral and written communication skills. Strong attention to detail, prioritization and time management skills

- Has sound understanding of sponsor/CRO business practices. Working knowledge of operational/financial practices, SOPs, GCPs, and FDA/ICH guidelines

Working Environment:
Thermo Fisher Scientific values the health and wellbeing of our employees. We support and encourage individuals to create a healthy and balanced environment where they can thrive. Below is listed the working environment/requirements for this role:
- Exposure to high pressure, intense concentration needed

- Must pay constant attention to detail-visual, mental

- Must be able to multi-task constantly

- Frequent interaction with clients / associates required

- Long, varied hours required occasionally

- Travel and rotating shifts required on rare occasions

Why join us?
When you join Thermo Fisher Scientific, you become part of a global team that values passion, innovation, and a commitment to scientific excellence. You’ll work in an environment where collaboration and development are part of the everyday experience—and where your contributions truly make a difference.

Apply today to help us deliver tomorrow’s breakthroughs.

jobs.title: Staff Program Manager, Clinical Sequencing CDx
jobs.description:
Work Schedule
Standard (Mon-Fri)
Environmental Conditions
Office
Job Description

When you’re part of the team at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you’ll do important work. And you’ll have the opportunity for continual growth and learning in a culture that empowers your development. With revenues of more than $40 billion and the largest investment in R&D in the industry, we give our people the resources and opportunities to make significant contributions to the world.

Location/Division-Specific Information:
Canfidate who can work on-site will be given preference. Relocation assistance is NOT provided.
*Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
*Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screen.

Discover Impactful Work:
Lead a portfolio of NGS-based oncology companion diagnostic programs that connect therapeutic development, clinical evidence, regulatory strategy, and patient access. As the Staff Program Manager, you will be accountable for moving programs from opportunity assessment and partner agreement through assay development, clinical and analytical validation, regulatory submission, launch, and lifecycle management. You will serve as the operating leader who creates clarity across a matrixed organization and turns complex science, partner requirements, and business commitments into reliable execution.

A day in the Life:
- Own integrated program strategy and execution for multiple companion diagnostic programs, including scope, critical path, decision points, resource needs, quality objectives, and launch readiness.
- Serve as Core Team Lead and the primary internal and external program contact for biopharma, biotechnology, CRO, clinical, and other strategic partners.
- Translate therapeutic, biomarker, clinical trial, and market requirements into executable product development plans with clear deliverables, decision rights, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
- Establish partner governance: define operating cadence, align expectations, negotiate and manage contractual and SOW commitments, document decisions, resolve escalations, and maintain trust through transparent communication.
- Lead cross-functional planning across assay and reagent development, bioinformatics and software, clinical and analytical validation, regulatory affairs, quality, manufacturing, supply chain, commercial, medical affairs, finance, and customer support.
- Lead regulatory and quality readiness from program start through submission and approval, partnering with Regulatory Affairs and Quality on design controls, risk management, traceability, verification and validation, change control, and health-authority responses.
- Coordinate clinical validation strategy and execution for regulatory-grade studies, partnering with Clinical and Regulatory Affairs to align therapeutic requirements, evidence plans, data-generation activities, and submission milestones.
- Build and manage integrated timelines, budgets, forecasts, resource plans, and applicable financial inputs. Surface tradeoffs early and recommend decisions that protect patient impact, partner commitments, quality, and business objectives.
- Create a single source of truth for program health through concise dashboards, milestone reviews, risk and dependency logs, decision records, and data-driven executive updates.
- Lead launch and post-launch readiness, including operational scalability, supply and manufacturing readiness, customer and commercial enablement, performance monitoring, and lifecycle improvements.
- Anticipate risk, frame options, and drive timely decisions when priorities, data, or stakeholder perspectives conflict.
- Influence senior technical and business leaders without formal authority, manage up effectively, and create accountability across internal teams and external partners.
- Communicate complex scientific, clinical, regulatory, and financial topics with precision to both expert and executive audiences.
- Bring structure to ambiguity while remaining adaptable as biomarker strategy, clinical data, partner needs, and regulatory expectations evolve.

Keys to Success:
Education
- Bachelor's degree in molecular biology, genetics, biochemistry, biomedical engineering, engineering, or a related scientific or technical discipline; advanced degree is a plus.
- A PMP or equivalent program management certification is preferred, but demonstrated delivery of complex regulated programs matters most.

Experience
- Typically 7+ years leading complex programs or product development in a regulated environment, including delivery of a diagnostic, IVD, medical device, clinical-testing product, or comparable regulated product. Biotechnology or pharmaceutical experience is relevant when paired with meaningful exposure to diagnostics or device programs.
- Demonstrated ownership of multiple cross-functional development programs from concept through validation, regulatory submission, launch, or lifecycle update, with clear accountability for decisions, risks, dependencies, and outcomes.
- Experience with oncology, precision medicine, NGS, molecular diagnostics, companion diagnostics, or a closely related clinical testing platform is preferred.
- Demonstrated experience managing strategic biopharma, biotechnology, customer, clinical, CRO, or technology-partner relationships, including expectation-setting, commitment negotiation, escalation management, and resolution of competing priorities across internal teams, clinical sites, laboratories, consultants, and vendors.
- Working knowledge of regulated product development sufficient to plan and govern execution, including 21 CFR Part 820 design controls, ISO 13485 principles, clinical/analytical validation, risk management, traceability, and quality systems.
- Experience building budgets, financial forecasts, business cases, revenue models, or P&L inputs for development programs is preferred.
- Proficiency with program-management tools and the ability to build integrated schedules that expose dependencies, resource constraints, and the true critical path.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
- Executive presence and outstanding written, verbal, and presentation skills.
- Strong judgment, prioritization, negotiation, and conflict-resolution skills.
- Ability to move fluidly between scientific detail, clinical evidence, regulatory requirements, operational execution, partner management, and business outcomes.
- High ownership, follow-through, and comfort being accountable for outcomes in a fast-moving, matrixed environment.

What Success Looks Like
- Partners and internal leaders have a clear, trusted view of program status, decisions, risks, and next milestones.
- Programs reach validation, regulatory, launch, and lifecycle milestones with predictable execution and appropriately managed tradeoffs.
- Clinical and regulatory evidence plans remain aligned to the therapeutic program and support timely patient access.
- The portfolio delivers measurable value through strong partner relationships, disciplined financial management, scalable operations, and high-quality products.

Benefits:
We offer competitive remuneration, annual incentive plan bonus, healthcare, and a range of employee benefits. Thermo Fisher Scientific offers employment with an innovative, forward-thinking organization, and outstanding career and development prospects. We offer an exciting company culture that stands for integrity, intensity, involvement, and innovation!

Compensation and Benefits
The salary range estimated for this position based in California is $113,500.00–$151,300.00.
This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:
- A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs

- Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement

- At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy

- Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan

- Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount

For more information on our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.thermofisher.com/global/en/total-rewards

At Thermo Fisher Scientific, our Finance teams are essential to our business and functional teams to make educated, sound decisions that drive our Mission and make us a stable and trusted industry leader. From Financial Planning & Analysis, Tax, Treasury, Financial Reporting, Audit, Investor Relations, Strategy & Corporate Development to Accounting, our Finance functions have a diverse and global presence, providing significant opportunities to develop unique career experiences and perspectives. Ranked #101 on the 2024 Fortune 500 list and with revenues of over $42 billion, you’ll discover endless opportunities to grow a rewarding career as part of the world leader serving science.

How you will make an impact:

The Finance Manager role will be responsible for Cost Accounting and Operations Finance projects within the global finance projects team. This role will collaborate in the Cost Accounting workstream to integrate a recent acquisition into Thermo Fisher’s E1 ERP environment, collaborate in the Cost Accounting workstream to transition sites from SAP ECC to SAP S/4HANA, and lead and collaborate on other cost accounting and Operations Finance projects across Thermo Fisher groups (e.g. LSG, LPG, BPG, SDG, and/or AIG).
This role will engage with finance leadership at group and division level to ensure a seamless execution of company, group, divisional and functional Operations Finance projects. This position will report to a Senior Finance Manager based in Singapore.

What you will do:

- Manage and develop a team of 0 to 3 direct reports to ensure we develop strategic partnerships as well as provide clear career paths
- Support the migration of entities into core company ERPs (e.g. E1 and SAP), with specific emphasis on migration to the manufacturing module
- Perform data validation and controls testing to ensure automated processes maintain accuracy, completeness, and compliance.  Troubleshoot and resolve issues during setup, testing, and go-live, and post go-live.
- Identify and ensure that business requirements are met within a project
- Troubleshoot and resolve issues during setup, testing, and go-live, and post go-live
- Provide updates to senior management with focus on decisions, issues, and risks
- Lead project related change management including communication and training
- Challenge the status quo, proactively identify and implement opportunities to leverage AI and automation, and/or collaborate with cross-functional partners (e.g. IT, COEs) to standardize processes, drive process improvements, and drive system enhancements.
- Collaborate to develop improved forecasting and reporting of Ops Finance KPIs (e.g. Power BI)
- Assess and implement opportunities to use AI / machine learning / generative AI tools to improve reporting efficiency, anomaly detection, root-cause analysis, and insight generation.
- Support ad-hoc internal, group, and corporate requests as needed.

How you will get here:

- Education Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Analytics, or Information Technology
- 5+ years relevant experience in finance
- Demonstrates and drives the Thermo Fisher values – Integrity, Intensity, Involvement and Innovation
- Track record of using tools such as Excel, Power Query, Power BI/Tableau, SQL, Python, Alteryx, Power Automate, or similar to automate workflows and improve financial reporting and analysis.
- Experience with ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, E1 (JD Edwards), Dynamics, etc.
- Cost Accounting and/or Operations Finance experience with knowledge of key accounting principles and financial reporting
- Experience working in a global, matrixed environment preferred
- Strong team building skills and ability to work with a diverse group of customers in a global-matrixed environment

jobs.description:

Job Description

At Thermo Fisher Scientific, our Finance teams play a critical role as an integral part of our business, ensuring that we are making the best allocation of financial resources, and sound business decisions. In doing so, we are able to most effectively drive our Mission and perform as an agile and trusted industry leader. From Financial Planning & Analysis, Tax, Treasury, Financial Reporting, Audit, Investor Relations, Strategy & Corporate Development to Accounting, our Finance functions have a diverse and global presence, providing significant opportunities to develop outstanding career experiences and perspectives. with revenues of more than $45 billion, you’ll discover endless opportunities to grow a rewarding career as part of the world leader serving science.

The Specialty Diagnostics Group (SDG) helps Thermo Fisher achieve its Mission by enabling human health care. We prioritize innovation with a clear purpose, aiming to improve clinicians' diagnostic capabilities and empower labs to make informed decisions, improve care quality, and provide timely answers throughout each individual's healthcare journey.

Position Summary:
The Senior Director, Finance will provide financial support for SDG. This position offers the right candidate an influential seat at the table of a growing and dynamic group and provides a substantial opportunity for career development and growth. Reporting to the Group VP, Finance this position will work closely with the Finance Leadership Team, and the Group and Division Presidents.

Key Responsibilities:
- Lead oversight, strategy, and execution for global SDG Group finance functions including FP&A, Finance Transformation, and strategic leadership in key finance and business projects. Supports development and implementation of overall Group Finance Strategy.
- Support the Group President, Group VP Finance and Group leadership team to set and deliver the annual, long range, and quarterly business plans and meet key operating & financial goals. Extended member of SDG Leadership Team.
- Strategic thought partner to the business with a focus on driving growth and value creation. Support business execution through active participation in key business strategy decisions including organic and inorganic Investments. Identify complex financial and business risks and develop mitigation strategies.
- Lead the core operating mechanisms, including the AOP, QBR/MBRs, and forecasts in collaboration with the leadership team, functional teams, and finance managers.
- Develop improved operational and technical controls through centralized Group level controls and targeted reporting enhancements within divisions.
- Partner with group leadership to evaluate acquisition and divestiture opportunities through robust due diligence, maximizing synergies and mitigating risks to support successful transaction execution.
- Maintain strong internal controls to safeguard company assets. Ensure alignment with local accounting standards and US GAAP.
- Partner with Group and Corporate Functional Leadership and to drive both functional and business operational improvements and efficiency.
- Develop analytical models and tools to drive growth initiatives and improve business decisions.
- Lead, hire, and develop group finance teams and partner with operating partners to develop enhanced skills and intuition for business.
- Set example for continuous operational improvement and drive efficiency across the business and functions.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities
- Strong analytical skills with attention to detail (emphasis on accuracy and timeliness) while being able to step back and analyze the overall business impact.
- Proven people and project management experience with successful results.
- Ability to work cross-functionally and lead by influence across a global organization.
- Outstanding leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills. Proven as an experienced, confident, and mature manager
- Track record of developing meaningful relationships at all levels within an organization – at both the business unit and divisional level and can operate effectively in a matrix reporting structure.
- Engaged leader who values frequent interactions and dialog with subordinates, peers, and the company's leadership team.
- Possess a strong set of personal and business values that coincide with those of our 4I values!
- Ability to thrive and lead in a complex business environment
- Ability to professionally present results and financial analysis to the Leadership Team.
- Able to define, quantify, and link the metrics used to measure progress on pivotal initiatives.

Job Requirements
- Bachelor’s Degree, preferably in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or Accounting. MBA preferred!
- 10+ years of experience in dynamic Finance roles including FP&A
- Solid understanding of Excel (i.e., financial models and analysis), Cognos reporting tool (or equivalent), PowerPoint, PowerBI and Hyperion Financial Management (HFM).
- Travel, up to 15%.

At Thermo Fisher Scientific, each one of our 130,000 extraordinary minds has a unique story to tell. Join us and contribute to our singular mission—enabling our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. Apply today http://jobs.thermofisher.com

Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status.

Job Description

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

About the Role:
As the Manufacturing Operations Manager, you will lead, direct and optimize manufacturing operations to safely deliver high-quality products on time, at the right cost, and in line with customer and business requirements. You will be accountable for operational performance across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Inventory, Productivity and People, while building the capability and capacity required to support sustainable business growth.

As a key member of the Site Leadership Team, you will translate business priorities into disciplined daily execution, develop high-performing production leaders and teams, and champion Practical Process Improvement (PPI), Lean Manufacturing, 5S and structured problem solving. You will partner closely with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Planning, Finance, Human Resources, EHS and other support functions to improve flow, strengthen operational reliability, increase customer responsiveness and create a culture of ownership, accountability and continuous improvement.

What You'll Do:
Safety, Health & Environment
- Lead and promote a strong Safety First culture across all manufacturing operations, ensuring safety is embedded in daily leadership, planning and decision-making.

- Ensure manufacturing activities comply with applicable workplace health, safety, environmental and regulatory requirements, as well as Thermo Fisher Scientific EHS standards.

- Drive proactive hazard identification, risk assessment, incident prevention and corrective-action closure within production areas.

- Participate in and support investigations of safety incidents and near misses, ensuring root causes are understood and sustainable corrective actions are implemented.

- Conduct regular safety engagement activities, workplace inspections and leadership safety walks, and ensure identified actions are closed in a timely manner.

- Ensure employees are trained, competent and authorized to perform work safely and in accordance with approved procedures and controls.

Manufacturing Operations
- Lead daily manufacturing operations to achieve site production, customer and business requirements across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost and Inventory.

- Ensure production schedules are executed safely, efficiently and in accordance with approved quality standards, work instructions and customer requirements.

- Optimize labor, equipment, production-cell and material utilization to maximize throughput, capacity utilization and operational efficiency.

- Develop and execute manufacturing plans that align labor, skills, work bays, tooling and production capacity with current demand and future growth requirements.

- Drive disciplined daily management through tier meetings, visual management, standard work, escalation and structured problem solving.

- Review operational performance, identify gaps and implement timely countermeasures to protect customer commitments and site objectives.

- Lead production supervisors, team leaders and manufacturing employees to deliver consistent shift-to-shift execution and strong operational handovers.

Quality Excellence
- Ensure products are manufactured in accordance with customer specifications, approved processes and applicable quality-system requirements.

- Partner with Quality and Engineering to strengthen process capability, product quality and Right First Time performance.

- Lead structured problem-solving, root cause analysis and corrective-action implementation for manufacturing quality issues.

- Reduce defects, scrap, rework, out-of-box failures and customer complaints through effective process controls, standard work and employee ownership.

- Support internal, customer and external audits and ensure manufacturing-related findings and actions are addressed effectively.

Operational Excellence, PPI, Lean Manufacturing & 5S
- Champion Practical Process Improvement (PPI), Lean Manufacturing and 5S principles across manufacturing operations.

- Develop, implement and sustain world-class 5S standards across production areas, including workplace organization, housekeeping, visual management and standard work.

- Establish regular 5S audits, ownership routines and corrective-action follow-up to ensure improvements are sustained.

- Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on waste elimination, improved flow, reduced cycle time, increased capacity and productivity improvement.

- Use Lean and PPI tools such as Value Stream Mapping, Kaizen, standard work, visual management, root cause analysis and problem-solving boards to improve end-to-end performance.

- Build employee capability and engagement in continuous improvement by coaching teams to identify problems, implement countermeasures and sustain gains.

- Partner with Engineering and Maintenance to improve equipment effectiveness, process reliability and manufacturing capability.

Leadership & People Development
- Lead, coach and develop production supervisors, team leaders and manufacturing employees to build a high-performance and highly engaged organization.

- Set clear expectations, establish accountability and ensure employees understand how their daily performance contributes to customer and site objectives.

- Conduct regular coaching, performance discussions and development planning, and address performance gaps in a timely and constructive manner.

- Develop succession plans, skills matrices, cross-training plans and talent pipelines to strengthen manufacturing capability and organizational resilience.

- Promote teamwork, respect, inclusion, ownership and continuous learning across the manufacturing organization.

- Ensure effective communication of business priorities, operational changes, performance results and key site messages to manufacturing teams.

Financial & Cost Management
- Manage manufacturing operations within approved budget and cost expectations while maintaining safety, quality and customer delivery performance.

- Drive productivity, labor-efficiency and cost-reduction initiatives and ensure benefits are measurable, validated and sustained.

- Monitor direct labor, overtime, manufacturing expenses and productivity performance and implement actions to address unfavorable trends.

- Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing profitability through better utilization, flow, standardization, automation and waste reduction.

- Support capital expenditure proposals and business cases for capacity, capability, safety, quality and productivity improvements.

Supply Chain, Inventory & Customer Delivery
- Partner with Planning and Supply Chain to ensure production plans are aligned with customer demand, material availability and site capacity.

- Improve schedule adherence, On-Time to Promise performance and backlog recovery through disciplined production planning and execution.

- Support inventory optimization, material-flow and inventory-accuracy initiatives while maintaining the materials required to protect customer delivery.

- Increase manufacturing responsiveness and flexibility to accommodate changing demand, product mix and customer priorities.

- Collaborate across functions to identify and mitigate production constraints, supplier risks and material shortages before they impact customers.

Maintenance & Asset Management
- Partner with Maintenance and Engineering to maximize equipment availability, production-cell reliability and manufacturing uptime.

- Support preventive and predictive maintenance programs and ensure production teams provide effective operational ownership and basic care of equipment.

- Participate in capital projects, equipment upgrades, new-product introductions and process-improvement initiatives that increase manufacturing capability and capacity.

- Ensure production equipment, tooling and work areas are maintained in a safe, organized and fit-for-purpose condition.

Stakeholder Management & Site Leadership
- Participate as a key member of the Site Leadership Team, contributing to site strategy, operating plans, capacity planning and business improvement priorities.

- Collaborate effectively with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Planning, Finance, Human Resources, EHS and other functions to deliver integrated site outcomes.

- Build strong working relationships with customers, suppliers, contractors and external stakeholders where required to support operational performance.

- Provide clear, concise and data-based updates to site leadership on manufacturing performance, risks, constraints, recovery plans and improvement priorities.

Education
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business or a related discipline; equivalent relevant experience will be considered.

- Postgraduate qualification in Operations Management, Engineering, Manufacturing or Business Administration is advantageous.

- Lean, PPI or Six Sigma certification is preferred; Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or higher is highly regarded.

Experience
- Minimum of 8-10 years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including significant experience in a complex or regulated manufacturing environment.

- Minimum of 5 years of leadership experience managing production teams, supervisors or team leaders with accountability for operational performance.

- Demonstrated success delivering improvements in Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Inventory and Productivity through disciplined operating systems and continuous improvement.

- Proven experience leading PPI, Lean Manufacturing, 5S, Kaizen or structured problem-solving initiatives and sustaining improvements over time.

- Experience managing performance through KPIs, tiered daily management, visual management and data-driven corrective actions.

- Experience leading cross-functional change, capacity expansion, operational recovery or manufacturing transformation initiatives.

- Experience with advanced, industrial, electronics, mining, defence, automotive, aerospace or similarly complex manufacturing environments is advantageous.

- Experience working in a global or matrix organization is preferred.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities
- Strong manufacturing-operations leadership capability with a practical understanding of production planning, labor management, capacity, flow, standard work and operational control.

- Strong working knowledge of PPI, Lean Manufacturing, 5S, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, root cause analysis and structured problem-solving methodologies.

- Demonstrated ability to translate business demand and customer priorities into executable production plans, resource requirements and operating rhythms.

- Strong understanding of quality management systems, process control, Right First Time principles and corrective-action governance within a regulated environment.

- Strong financial and commercial acumen, including budget management, labor productivity, cost control, capital justification and benefit tracking.

- Working knowledge of ERP/MRP systems, production scheduling, inventory management and operational data analysis.

- Strong leadership and coaching skills with the ability to build accountability, engagement, capability and a culture of continuous improvement.

- Excellent problem-solving, prioritization and decision-making skills, with the ability to remain effective under changing priorities and operational pressure.

- Strong stakeholder-management, influencing and communication skills, including the ability to align cross-functional teams and communicate effectively at all levels.

- Ability to analyze operational data and metrics, identify trends and constraints, and translate findings into clear actions and measurable outcomes.

- Strong digital literacy, including Microsoft Office and relevant manufacturing, planning, reporting and data-visualization systems.

- Embodies Thermo Fisher Scientific's 4i values of Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement.

Benefits
Join our team and take advantage of these great benefits! Apply now to learn more about the full range of benefits we offer.
- Health & Wellbeing: Join a company that prioritizes your health & wellbeing with comprehensive benefits, wellness programs, and an Employee Assistance Program providing confidential support for personal and work-related issues.

Lead commercial contract negotiations, strategic projects, and continuous improvement initiatives across Taiwan's Distribution & Logistics network. Own the negotiation and renewal of 3PL, customs broker, and freight forwarder contracts, driving favorable commercial terms and service structures. Partner cross-functionally to lead structural projects — network footprint evaluation, cost optimization, and process redesign — that improve D&L's operational efficiency and support long-term business planning. - Lead negotiation and renewal of contracts with 3PLs, customs brokers, and freight forwarders, owning commercial terms, rate structures, and service category definitions.

- Own the D&L continuous improvement / PPI(Lean) agenda — identifying inefficiencies across the network, driving standardization, automation, and cost-reduction initiatives.
- Establish a structured framework for tracking CI initiative outcomes and cost impact.
- Benchmark against other regional markets (e.g., Japan, China, Singapore, Korea) to identify improvement opportunities applicable to Taiwan.

- Work closely with the Logistics Lead and Trade Operation Supervisor to ensure negotiated commercial terms align with day-to-day operational and compliance requirements.

- Excellent negotiation, stakeholder management, and project management skills.
- Proficient in English and Mandarin Chinese (spoken and written).

Preferred

- Familiarity with trade compliance and import/export cost structures (duty, landed cost) sufficient to collaborate effectively with the Trade Operation Supervisor.
- Experience with ERP/WMS systems and Microsoft Office Suite (advanced Excel/analytics).

Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. is the world leader in serving science, with annual revenue exceeding $40 billion. Our mission is to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer. From advancing life sciences research and solving complex analytical challenges to improving diagnostics and driving laboratory efficiency, we empower our customers with innovative technologies and services.
Within Thermo Fisher, our Global Business Services (GBS) Shared Services team is transforming how we work, optimizing processes, and driving productivity. With over 2300+ colleagues across five global locations, including our Sofia site, we deliver scalable, cost-effective solutions. Since its establishment in 2013, the Sofia Finance Shared Services center has been operating for over 10 years with a proven track of record of success and growth and is designed to serve our global customers across various financial functions, including Procure to Pay, Record to Report and Order to Cash.
Key   Responsibilities:
- Provide strategic and operational leadership to the global Accounts Payable teams, including regional teams, supervisors, and senior specialists.
- Oversee end-to-end AP operations, ensuring accurate and timely processing of invoices, payments, and vendor queries across multiple legal entities and regions.
- Develop, implement, and monitor SLAs, KPIs, and performance dashboards to ensure operational excellence and accountability.
- Drive global process standardization, automation (e.g., RPA, AI-enabled OCR), and continuous improvement across invoice-to-pay processes.
- Collaborate with Procurement, Finance, Treasury, and Compliance teams to optimize P2P performance, working capital, and risk management.
- Ensure adherence to internal controls (SOX), tax and regulatory requirements, and corporate policies, especially in highly regulated environments (e.g., clinical research).
- Manage internal and external audit requirements; support statutory, group, and management reporting as needed.
- Lead and develop a high-performing AP team; coach and mentor direct reports and identify future leadership talent.
- Lead or support global transformation projects, ERP rollouts, business transitions, and M&A integrations.
- Represent the AP function in governance forums, business reviews, and stakeholder engagements at senior levels.

Basic Requirements :
- University degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or related discipline; professional certification (e.g., ACCA, CPA, CIMA) preferred.
- 8–10 years of progressive experience in Accounts Payable or P2P, with at least 3 years in a people management or leadership role.
- Strong understanding of global P2P operating models, controls, compliance frameworks (e.g., SOX, GDPR), and tax implications (e.g., VAT, WHT).
- Proven experience managing large, distributed teams in a shared services or multinational environment.
- Demonstrated ability to lead process optimization, automation, and change initiatives.
- Strong interpersonal, stakeholder management, and communication skills, with experience engaging senior leadership and cross-functional partners.
- ERP proficiency (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Coupa, Ariba) and familiarity with payment and invoice automation tools.

jobs.description:
Work Schedule
Standard (Mon-Fri)
Environmental Conditions
Office
Job Description

Job Description
At Thermo Fisher Scientific, our Finance teams partner with the business to understand performance, provide insights, and support decisions that help advance our Mission. Our global organization offers opportunities to build broad business experience and grow a rewarding career with the world leader in serving science.

Location / Division Specific Information
This position will preferably be based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Candidates based in Waltham, Massachusetts may also be considered.
The role supports the Asset Management Services business within Instrument and Enterprise Services. Asset Management Services is a global services business, and this position will have primary financial responsibility for supporting the European business, along with responsibilities across the broader global organization.
The position offers meaningful exposure to an international business and the opportunity to partner with Commercial, Operations, Accounting, and Finance colleagues across functions and geographies.

How You Will Make an Impact
We are seeking a Senior Financial Analyst who is ready to take greater ownership and accountability while developing a deeper understanding of the business behind the numbers.
You will own key financial reporting, forecasting, planning, and performance analysis, with accountability for delivering accurate, timely, and meaningful financial insights. You will develop a strong understanding of the commercial and operational drivers of the business, identify risks and opportunities, and help translate financial performance into actions.
Working across Finance, Commercial, Operations, and Accounting, you will help drive financial discipline and accountability, ensuring performance gaps are understood, actions are followed through, and leaders have the insights needed to make sound business decisions.
This is an opportunity to own meaningful work, gain global business exposure, and build the financial and business partnering experience for continued career growth.

What You Will Do
- Own key financial reporting, forecasting, and performance analysis, with accountability for the accuracy, quality, and timeliness of financial information.
- Analyze performance against forecast, plan, and prior periods to identify business drivers, trends, risks, and opportunities.
- Partner with Commercial and Operations teams to understand revenue, profitability, expenses, business pacing, and other drivers of performance.
- Translate financial and operational data into clear insights that help the business understand what happened, why it happened, and what actions are needed next.
- Drive follow-through on financial commitments by highlighting performance gaps, appropriately challenging assumptions, and helping business partners maintain accountability for agreed actions.
- Support monthly forecasting, annual planning, and long-term planning processes, ensuring assumptions are well understood and appropriately supported.
- Partner with Accounting during the monthly close to ensure the integrity of financial results, investigate unusual items, support accruals, and resolve financial reporting issues.
- Build financial models and provide analysis supporting pricing, expenses, headcount, investments, and other business decisions.
- Identify opportunities to simplify and automate reporting, forecasting, and analytical processes to improve efficiency and insight.

How You Will Get Here

Education
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field.

Experience
- 3+ years of relevant Finance experience, preferably in financial planning and analysis, commercial finance, or business finance.
- Strong financial and analytical skills, including forecasting, budgeting, reporting, variance analysis, and financial modeling.
- Experience with enterprise resource planning systems, financial reporting or planning tools, and Microsoft Excel. Experience with SAP, Hyperion Planning, Power BI, Cognos, or similar platforms is beneficial.
- Strong communication and business partnering skills, with the ability to translate financial analysis into clear insights and build relationships across functions and geographies.
- Demonstrated curiosity, ownership, and accountability, with the confidence to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and consistently deliver high-quality work.

What Will Make You Successful
You are curious, accountable, and motivated to understand the business behind the numbers. You take ownership of your work, follow through on commitments, and investigate when something does not look right.
You don't stop at identifying a variance—you work to understand the cause, communicate the impact, and help ensure the right actions are taken.
You want to use Finance to help drive better decisions, stronger financial discipline, and accountability across the business.
This role provides the opportunity to own meaningful work, develop a global perspective, build strong business partnerships, and continue growing your Finance career at Thermo Fisher Scientific.

Travel Requirements
Less than 5% domestic and international travel required.

Compensation and Benefits
The salary range estimated for this position based in Pennsylvania is $93,800.00–$140,675.00.
This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:
- A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs

- Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement

- At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy

- Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan

- Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount

For more information on our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.thermofisher.com/global/en/total-rewards

(CIS) Corporate Infrastructure and Security M&A Synergy Analyst

We are seeking a dedicated and collaborative professional to partner with Thermo Fisher  Scientific's Corporate Infrastructure and Security (CIS) teams across M&A, Service Delivery,  Finance, and Sourcing to identify, track, and drive synergy and cost-saving opportunities across  M&A programs and projects.

This individual will play a key role in establishing and operationalizing new processes to support chargeback management across CIS, while developing a streamlined and automated approach for tracking M&A transactions, software licensing, and optimization opportunities.

The role will  coordinate governance activities and cross-functional updates among Finance, Sourcing, Service Delivery, M&A, and Synergy Program teams to ensure process adoption, financial transparency,  and chargeback accuracy.

In addition, this position will support the execution of CIS's Executive Business Review (EBR) program, partnering with strategic vendors to facilitate discussions around integration planning,  technology roadmaps, contract optimization, and software licensing strategies that maximize  business value.

The preferred work location for this role is on-site in Frederick, Maryland.

Responsibilities :
• Collaborate with Finance, M&A, and Service Delivery teams to establish a chargeback management approach across CIS, leveraging existing frameworks while ensuring ongoing governance and compliance.

- Deliver ongoing support for assigned Accounts Payable process areas, ensuring consistent service delivery and operational excellence across the end-to-end P2P process.

- Ensure compliance with corporate policies, audit requirements, SOX requirements, and VAT rules.

- Contribute to the stabilization of new P2P processes after go-live, and support the transition to business-as-usual
- Other tasks as assigned

- Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or Business Administration is preferred.
- Proven experience in Accounts Payable or a related finance role, with a focus on Procure To Pay (P2P) processes.
- Solid understanding of accounting principles, practices, and regulations.
- Proficiency in AP software and ERP systems.
- Fluent in English is required, both written and spoken – fluency in German and/or French is highly desirable.

Skills Required:

- Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, ensure timely delivery, coordinate stakeholders, and monitor progress effectively.
- Advanced analytical skills, including the ability to interpret large data sets, identify trends and discrepancies, and apply insights to drive effective solutions.
- Effective collaboration skills, with the ability to work across procurement, finance, IT, and other stakeholders, building productive relationships
- High adaptability, with the ability to adjust quickly to shifting priorities and transition efficiently between tasks, teams or projects based on business needs.
- Continuous improvement mindset, proactively identifying opportunities to enhance processes, reduce inefficiencies, and implement best practices across the P2P cycle.

We are seeking a Senior Staff Program Manager to join our Electron Microscopy Research & Development organization. In this strategic leadership role, you will lead complex, cross-functional technology programs within the Semiconductor Business Unit from concept through commercialization.

You will work closely with R&D, Operations, Service, Product Marketing, Quality, Regulatory, and other key partners to deliver advanced electron microscopy products and solutions to customers around the world. This role requires strong technical program leadership, excellent stakeholder management, disciplined execution, and the ability to drive alignment across global, matrixed teams.

This is an opportunity to shape product development programs that support some of the world’s most advanced scientific and industrial workflows, including life sciences research, materials analysis, and semiconductor manufacturing.

What You Will Do
- Lead large-scale, multi-disciplinary programs from concept through development, launch, and commercialization.
- Establish and manage program governance, including scope, milestones, budgets, resources, risks, decision forums, and executive reporting.
- Partner with R&D, Operations, Service, Product Marketing, Quality, Regulatory, and other stakeholders to ensure successful product development and launch readiness.

- Ensure program activities are conducted in alignment with applicable quality, regulatory, and compliance standards.
- Manage multiple high-priority initiatives simultaneously in a fast-paced, global environment.
- Report status of the program to stakeholders and management on regular reviews.

How You Will Make an Impact
In this role, you will help turn advanced technology ideas into customer-ready solutions. Your work will help ensure that complex electron microscopy programs move efficiently from R&D into products that can be manufactured, launched, supported, and used by customers globally.

By bringing structure, clarity, and cross-functional alignment to highly technical programs, you will help Thermo Fisher deliver innovations that enable customers to make critical discoveries, improve product quality, advance semiconductor and materials research, and accelerate scientific progress.

What You Bring

- Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Physics, Life Sciences, Business Administration, or a related technical field with 8+ years of experience in program management within complex technical environments; or advanced degree with 6+ years of relevant experience.
- Proven experience leading large-scale, cross-functional technical programs from concept through delivery.

Job Description

Here at Thermo Fisher Scientific, our industry-leading scale means unparalleled commercial reach, unique customer access and a global footprint. Our broad customer base, from research, clinical to commercial production means you can have a broad and significant impact. All while working in an environment where you will be supported, valued and rewarded for your performance. Join our Sales team with an unmatched depth of capabilities and help our customers solve some of the world’s toughest challenges.

Location/Division Specific Information
The Immunodiagnostics Division ( IDD ) of Thermo Fisher Scientific strives to improve the management of allergy, asthma, and autoimmune diseases by providing healthcare professionals with advanced diagnostics technologies and clinical expertise. Our key businesses: allergy, autoimmunity, and systems.

Location: This is a field-based position supporting customers across the Southeast: Florida, Alabama, Mississippi and parts of Southern Georgia with significant regional travel required.
Residency within local territory required. No relocation assistance will be provided.

A day in the Life:
- Lead a team of Clinical Sales Specialists to coordinate the tactical plans needed to drive allergy growth within assigned district.
- Recruit, hire, coach, lead, train and develop a highly-talented sales staff to build a strong, and motivated work team.
- Develop the District strategy and tactics to increase utilization of allergy testing to achieve 100%+.
- Responsible for the orchestration and proper use of available resources to act on opportunities for growth and optimized lab utilization.
- Lead the team to grow their territory with initiatives once commitment is received from national and regional reference labs and health systems.
- Develop and cultivate advocacy to drive sales and market growth collaborating with established customer assignment.
- Provide business insight and value to retain customer and enhance customer relationships.
- Persuasively articulate the clinical and economic case for expanded testing at the highest executive levels within these institutions and to have a working knowledge of the dynamics of healthcare delivery.
- Participate in company meetings for training purposes, product information updates, and sharing field intelligence information.
- Assist with growth and development of the sales team by providing training, guidance & assistance.

Education
- Bachelor's Degree required, within Business or Healthcare related field preferred.

Experience
- 7+ years sales experience in healthcare, pharmaceutical, medical diagnostic, medical device sales and/or sales management; OR documented career progression within industry including management development.
- 3+ years of successful people leadership experience
- Experience operating effectively in complex, matrixed organizations.

- Demonstrated leadership skills focused on creating successful work environments.
- Develops a high-performing commercial team focused on individualized development plans.
- Successfully attracts, develops, and retains highly qualified sales professionals that contribute to the success of Thermo Fisher Scientific.
- Committed to maintaining a culture of open communication, transparency, diversity, and inclusion. Continuously fostering a strong sense of belonging.
- Proficient in critical thinking, strategic business planning, and execution to meet and exceed our goals.
- Leverages strong analytical skills and a continuous improvement mindset.
- Consistently oversees and is accountable for the sales team’s results in the district.
- Drives strong commercial rigor to ensure accurate sales forecasting, pipeline management, and sales tracking through Salesforce CRM and other designated IT tools.
- Exhibits excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to communicate with diverse customer audiences such as scientific leaders, researchers, procurement, lab operations, economic decision-makers, and other influencers to gain commitment, acquire resources and achieve desired results.
- Uses extensive knowledge of customer activities and goals to develop high-impact strategic selling presentations promoting Thermo Fisher Scientific solutions.
- Develops and maintains up-to-date knowledge of consumable and instrument technologies, products, services, markets, and customer buying practices required to manage a sales team to be successful effectively.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities
- Gets Results: Consistently achieving results even under tough circumstances.
- Customers : Building strong customer relationships and delivering customer-centric solutions.

- Communicates Effectively : Developing and delivering communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.
- Instills Trust : Gaining the confidence and trust of others through honesty, integrity and authenticity.
- Ability to travel 60 – 80% extensively throughout the district. Relocation assistance is NOT provided.
- Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
- Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

Job Description

Thermo Fisher Scientific’s Immunodiagnostics Division (IDD) is dedicated to improving the management of allergy, asthma, and autoimmune diseases through advanced diagnostic technologies and deep clinical expertise. With a broad global footprint and unmatched commercial scale, our teams help healthcare partners solve some of the world’s toughest challenges while improving patient outcomes.

Position Summary
The Business Development Executive (BDE) is responsible for driving growth within Health System, Hospital, Regional Reference Lab, and National Account segments by advancing the adoption, implementation, and consistent utilization of IDD diagnostic testing solution. This role owns the transition from customer onboarding through revenue realization and develops strategies that optimize lab utilization, expand testing menus, and increase pull-through in high-opportunity markets.

The BDE will persuasively articulate the clinical and economic value of expanded testing to senior executive stakeholders and serve as the primary orchestrator of internal commercial resources to accelerate growth, driving adoption of full diagnostic menus and evidence-based allergy and autoimmune panels.

Territory Coverage: This role supports Florida, Kentucky, Tennessee, Alabama, and Georgia and requires travel throughout the assigned territory.

Key Responsibilities
Strategic Account Growth & Market Development
- Lead the advancement of IDD test adoption within hospitals and large healthcare organizations from implementation through revenue generation.
- Identify, qualify, and pursue new business opportunities across allergy, autoimmune, and adjacent diagnostic markets, including urgent care and retail health centers.
- Develop and execute strategic and tactical plans to increase testing volume, optimize menu utilization, and support health system expansion initiatives.
- Evaluate customer needs, provide actionable business insights, and cultivate long-term customer advocacy that drives sustained growth.

Executive-Level Engagement & Value Communication
- Persuasively communicate the clinical utility and economic value proposition of IDD testing to C-suite executives, business leaders, and clinical decision makers.
- Demonstrate a strong understanding of healthcare delivery systems, reimbursement dynamics, laboratory operations, and payer/provider economics.
- Develop and present compelling business cases to support expanded testing adoption within IDNs, GPOs, ACOs, and regional health systems.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Resource Alignment
- Serve as the key liaison between customers and the internal commercial organization, ensuring appropriate resource deployment and seamless execution.
- Partner closely with Strategic Account Managers (SAMs), Strategic Account Executives (SAEs), Regional Managers, Clinical Sales Specialists (CSS), and Demand Generation leadership (DM) to activate coordinated growth initiatives.
- Collaborate with marketing, sales operations, and product teams to support aligned messaging and targeted campaigns.
- Participate in ongoing training, field intelligence sharing, and performance reviews related to account strategy.

Sales Execution & Performance Management
- Meet or exceed assigned sales and growth targets through disciplined pipeline management and strategic selling practices.
- Independently develop and execute strategies while effectively leading cross-functional teams without formal authority.
- Maintain accurate account planning, forecasting, and reporting aligned to commercial objectives.
- Promote strong customer relationships through proactive communication, problem-solving, and customer-first engagement.

Education & Experience Requirements
Education
- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Healthcare, or a related field.

Experience
- 8+   years of successful sales or business development experience in healthcare, diagnostics, laboratory services, or pharmaceuticals.
- Proven success exceeding sales targets while navigating complex selling environments.
- Demonstrated experience developing strategies that drive measurable growth in healthcare systems or diagnostic markets.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
- Deep understanding of healthcare delivery systems, reimbursement models, provider/payer economics, laboratory and hospital/IDN dynamics.
- Strong communication, negotiation, and presentation skills, able to influence at all organizational levels, including C-suite, both virtually and in-person.
- Creative, solutions-oriented approach with the ability to operate independently while collaborating effectively across a matrix organization.
- Strong organizational skills, project management capabilities, and attention to detail.
- Demonstrated ability to lead without authority and coordinate resources to achieve shared targets.
- Customer-focused mindset with outstanding listening skills and a passion for delivering value.
- Resilient, flexible, and capable of navigating evolving business needs.
- Travel required 50-75% within territory.

Why Join Us?

The   General Management Graduate Leadership Development Program (GM GLDP)   is an accelerated opportunity to develop the vital competencies and experiences   needed   for a career as a General Manager.

As a global company with opportunities spanning multiple businesses, functions, and locations, applicants   are required to   be geographically flexible and mobile for the   GM GLDP   and post-program. Rotational assignments and full-time placements are based on business needs and organizational priorities at the time of selection.   Onsite and in-office work is an essential function of this role and a requirement of the position.

Strategic Business Impact

The   GM   GLDP   is a   three - year program   set to occur between   Ju ly  12 , 2027 –   July 2030 .   Participants will complete three, twelve-month rotations that provide strategic direction while gaining   proficiency   with our diverse functional areas, business units, and regions. Learning opportunities will   include:   formal development sessions ,   dedicated Executive Mentorship ,   utilization   of our Practical Process Improvement (PPI)   methodology ,   and a network of outstanding LDP alumni. Critical capabilities for the   GM GLDP   include:

- Balancing   Financial   and   Business   Levers

- Commercial Acumen

- Product or Service Management

- End-to-End Operations

Compensation

Our   GM GLDP   offers a starting salary of   $165,000   in addition to the following as part of the total compensation: Annual Incentive Plan, Sign-on Bonus, Equity Grant,   and   Relocation Assistance .

What We Look For

Academic Background & Work Experience:

- MBA   student completing their   degree between   December 202 6   – June 202 7   with an Undergraduate degree in one of the following: Business, Biology, Bioengineering, Biomedical Engineering, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Economics, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, or related field of study.

- 3+ years   (5+ preferred)   work experience post-Undergraduate degree – ideally gained in large, forward-thinking, global organizations. Experience in Life Sciences or STEM-related industry   required .

- 1+   years   experience   managing direct reports.

Leadership Profile:

- Proven leadership experience with   a track record   of influencing others, leading initiatives, driving results, and creating positive impact within teams and organizations.

- Demonstrated ability to navigate ambiguity, adapt to changing priorities, and solve complex problems.

- Evidence of grit, resilience, and perseverance when facing challenges, setbacks, or competing priorities.

- Strong learning agility, intellectual curiosity, and an innovative mindset.

- Excellent interpersonal communication skills and emotional intelligence, with the ability to build relationships across diverse teams.

- Geographic mobility and flexibility   required   to pursue future career opportunities in locations aligned with business needs.

- Onsite and in-office work is an essential function of this role and is   required   throughout the program and in future placements to support collaboration across businesses, functions, and locations.

If this sounds like you,   we'd   love to hear from you!

To qualify, applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States and should not require sponsorship (current or future) for employment visa status. jobs.title: Strategic Partnership and Business Development Manager
jobs.description:
Work Schedule
Standard (Mon-Fri)
Environmental Conditions
Office
Job Description

DESCRIPTION:
Join our team at Thermo Fisher Scientific where you'll contribute to business growth and strategic partnerships across key markets. As Sales Development Manager, you'll identify opportunities while building strong relationships with customers in sectors including pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, semiconductors, and academic research. You'll develop and implement comprehensive market strategies, coordinate cross-functional initiatives, and provide solutions that help our customers make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. This role offers the opportunity to work with advanced scientific technologies while collaborating with colleagues across our organization.

Position Purpose
•    Identify and develop high-impact growth opportunities that require capabilities across multiple Thermo Fisher Scientific divisions.
•    Serve as the enterprise business development leader and cross-division orchestrator, connecting customer priorities with Thermo Fisher capabilities to create differentiated One Thermo Fisher value propositions.
•    Lead strategic opportunities from early identification through internal alignment, solution development, executive engagement, commercial strategy, and opportunity conversion.

Key Responsibilities
1. Strategic Business Development
•    Identify and develop high-value growth opportunities across strategic customers, industries, applications, and emerging markets, with emphasis on complex and cross-divisional opportunities.
•    Support the development of country 5 years STRAP plan to accelerate sustainable growth.
•    Translate customer strategies, investment priorities, technology roadmaps, research programs, and unmet needs into qualified business opportunities and strategic business cases.
•    Build and manage a portfolio of strategic opportunities from concept through customer engagement, solution development, commercial alignment, and conversion.
2. Cross-Division/Corporate Opportunity Development
•    Proactively identify opportunities that require products, technologies, services, or expertise from multiple Thermo Fisher divisions.
•    Bring together division leaders, commercial teams, technical experts, marketing, applications, and service around a common customer opportunity and shared business objective.
•    Establish clear roles, ownership, contribution models, and execution plans while resolving gaps, overlaps, and internal barriers.
3. One Thermo Fisher Value Proposition
•    Lead the development of integrated customer value propositions that combine Thermo Fisher technologies, workflows, services, expertise, and commercial capabilities.
•    Shift customer engagement from individual products toward complete workflows, enterprise solutions, and strategic outcomes, articulating Why Thermo Fisher, Why Together, Why Now, and What Unique Value We Enable.
•    Quantify and differentiate customer value through productivity, workflow efficiency, quality, speed, scientific capability, cost optimization, risk reduction, and strategic impact.
4. Cross-Division Engagement & Alignment
•    Act as the neutral enterprise orchestrator, creating alignment across divisions around customer priorities, strategic opportunities, competitive positioning, and proposed solutions.
•    Facilitate cross-divisional strategy discussions, establish shared success criteria, and address ownership gaps, competing priorities, or execution barriers.
•    Ensure Thermo Fisher presents one coordinated customer strategy by connecting Taiwan, regional, and global capabilities where required.
5. Strategic Customer Opportunity Creation
•    Engage senior customer stakeholders to understand long-term priorities, investment plans, workflows, strategic programs, and future capability requirements.
•    Identify white-space opportunities beyond existing product discussions where Thermo Fisher can expand its strategic relevance and share of customer.
•    Convert customer priorities into defined cross-divisional opportunities, multi-year growth roadmaps, and executive engagement plans.
6. Enterprise Solution & Workflow Development
•    Map Thermo Fisher capabilities against the customer’s complete workflow, strategic objective, or business challenge to identify opportunities for integrated solutions.
•    Partner with technical and commercial teams to combine capabilities across divisions and address gaps through internal capabilities, partnerships, or new business models.
•    Develop repeatable enterprise solution frameworks and commercial models that can be scaled across strategic accounts and market segments.
7. Strategic Partnership Development
•    Identify strategic partners that strengthen Thermo Fisher’s ability to access markets, complete workflows, develop differentiated solutions, or accelerate opportunity conversion.
•    Establish outcome-driven partnerships with customers, research institutions, government organizations, technology providers, and ecosystem stakeholders.
•    Link partnerships directly to measurable business outcomes, including market development, capability enhancement, strategic pipeline, and revenue creation.
8. Market & Opportunity Intelligence
•    Monitor customer investments, emerging applications, technology trends, industry developments, government initiatives, and competitive activities to identify future growth opportunities.
•    Translate market intelligence and early customer signals into specific business-development hypotheses and cross-divisional opportunity maps.
•    Provide leadership with actionable recommendations on where Thermo Fisher should engage, invest, partner, or develop new value propositions.
9. Opportunity Governance & Execution
•    Establish disciplined governance for major strategic opportunities, including objectives, participating divisions, sponsors, owners, milestones, dependencies, and next actions.
•    Conduct regular cross-divisional reviews, track opportunities from creation through commercial conversion, and escalate barriers requiring leadership intervention.
•    Capture lessons learned and replicate successful cross-divisional business-development models across customers, segments, and strategic markets.

Role Mission: Identify high-value strategic opportunities, align Thermo Fisher capabilities across divisions, and convert them into differentiated One Thermo Fisher value propositions that create measurable customer value and incremental business growth.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. Master’s degree in Life Sciences, Chemistry, Engineering, Business, or a related field, with 8+ years of relevant sales, strategic business development, or commercial experience in life sciences, analytical instrumentation, healthcare, or related industries.
2. Demonstrated success in developing and executing strategic business development and growth plans, identifying new opportunities, building qualified pipelines, and delivering measurable revenue growth.
3. Proven ability to lead complex, cross-divisional and cross-functional opportunities, aligning commercial, technical, marketing, service, and leadership stakeholders around shared customer objectives and a One Thermo Fisher value proposition.
4. Strong understanding of customer workflows, applications, scientific technologies, market dynamics, and laboratory operations, with the ability to translate customer strategic priorities into integrated business opportunities.
5. Excellence in establishing and maintaining senior-level customer relationships, including key decision-makers, influencers, strategic partners, and executive stakeholders.
6. Strong strategic thinking, commercial acumen, analytical, and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to develop compelling business cases, opportunity strategies, and differentiated value propositions.
7. Advanced communication, executive presentation, influencing, and negotiation skills, with the ability to simplify complex concepts and gain alignment across diverse internal and external stakeholders.
8. Demonstrated ability to influence without direct authority and operate effectively within a complex global matrix organization, balancing divisional priorities while driving enterprise-level outcomes.
9. Strong project leadership and execution capabilities, with experience coordinating multiple stakeholders, managing strategic initiatives, establishing priorities, and driving opportunities from concept through commercial execution.
10. Proficiency with CRM platforms and Microsoft Office applications, with strong organizational, opportunity-management, and data-driven decision-making capabilities.
11. Fluency in English required, with the ability to communicate effectively with regional and global stakeholders.
12. Ability and willingness to travel up to 50% based on customer, partner, and business requirements.

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

This role will support our CMD Commercial and Marketing functions. From sample to knowledge to results, the Chromatography and Mass Spectrometry business develops and manufactures leading-edge chromatography and mass spectrometry instruments, consumables, and software solutions for customers working in the analytical sciences (routine testing markets) and scientific research. Our complete workflow solutions enable productivity and efficiency for customers performing food and beverage testing and manufacturing, environmental and industrial testing, biopharma QA/QC, toxicology, and anti-doping. For scientific research customers, our products support a range of focus areas, including proteomics, metabolomics, drug discovery, and clinical research.
